rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customers_cohort AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  NULL AS initial_balance
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id FROM customer_nodes
  UNION
  SELECT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
)
),
customer_monthly_closing_balances AS (
SELECT
  cc.customer_id AS customer_id,
  strftime('%Y', rm.month_start) AS year,
  strftime('%m', rm.month_start) AS month,
  rm.month_end AS month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance: sum of initial_balance + all txn_amounts up to month_end_date
  COALESCE(
    cc.initial_balance,
    0
  )
  +
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(ct.txn_amount)
    FROM customer_transactions ct
    WHERE ct.customer_id = cc.customer_id
      AND date(ct.txn_date) <= date(rm.month_end)
  ), 0) AS closing_balance,
  -- month_over_month_change: closing_balance minus prior month's closing_balance
  (
    (
      COALESCE(cc.initial_balance,0)
      +
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(ct2.txn_amount)
        FROM customer_transactions ct2
        WHERE ct2.customer_id = cc.customer_id
          AND date(ct2.txn_date) <= date(rm.month_end)
      ),0)
    )
    -
    (
      COALESCE(cc.initial_balance,0)
      +
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(ct3.txn_amount)
        FROM customer_transactions ct3
        WHERE ct3.customer_id = cc.customer_id
          AND date(ct3.txn_date) <= date(date(rm.month_start, '-1 day'))
      ),0)
    )
  ) AS month_over_month_change,
  -- cumulative_balance: running sum of closing_balance across months per customer
  (
    SELECT SUM(
      COALESCE(cc2.initial_balance,0)
      +
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(ct4.txn_amount)
        FROM customer_transactions ct4
        WHERE ct4.customer_id = cc.customer_id
          AND date(ct4.txn_date) <= date(rm2.month_end)
      ),0)
    )
    FROM customers_cohort cc2
    JOIN (
      -- generate same report months rows via recursive approach substitution:
      -- but to keep view self-contained, assume there exists same months in customers_cohort join space
      -- replicate rows by selecting distinct month starts/ends from a calendar derived from transactions and node dates
      SELECT DISTINCT
        date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date))) AS month_start,
        date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
      FROM customer_transactions t
      UNION
      SELECT DISTINCT
        date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date))) AS month_start,
        date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
      FROM customer_nodes
    ) rm2 ON 1=1
    WHERE cc2.customer_id = cc.customer_id
      AND (date(rm2.month_end) <= date(rm.month_end))
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customers_cohort cc
-- derive report months calendar by union of months present in data to ensure every month in reporting period is present
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date))) AS month_start,
    date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
  FROM customer_transactions t
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date))) AS month_start,
    date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
  FROM customer_nodes
) rm ON 1=1
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  m.year,
  m.month,
  m.month_end_date,
  cmb.closing_balance,
  cmb.month_over_month_change,
  cmb.cumulative_balance
FROM customers_cohort AS c
CROSS JOIN (
  -- generate months between start and end dates inclusive
  WITH params AS (
    SELECT date('2020-01-01') AS start_date, date('2020-12-31') AS end_date
  ),
  months AS (
    SELECT
      strftime('%Y', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) AS year,
      CAST(strftime('%m', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) AS INTEGER) AS month,
      date(strftime('%Y', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) || '-' ||
           strftime('%m', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) || '-01', '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date
    FROM params,
         (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
          UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
          UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
          UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
          UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
          UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
          UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
          UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
          UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
          UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
          UNION ALL SELECT 60) AS nums
    WHERE date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months') <= params.end_date
  )
  SELECT year, month, month_end_date FROM months
) AS m
LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_closing_balances AS cmb
  ON cmb.customer_id = c.customer_id
  AND cmb.year = CAST(m.year AS INTEGER)
  AND cmb.month = m.month
ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC, m.year ASC, m.month ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH all_customers_months_2020 AS (
SELECT
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(months.month_start) AS month_start_date,
  strftime('%Y-%m', months.month_start) || '-01' AS month_label
FROM
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
    FROM customer_nodes
  ) AS c
CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT '2020-01-01' AS month_start UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-02-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-03-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-04-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-05-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-06-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-07-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-08-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-09-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-10-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-11-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-12-01'
  ) AS months
),
customer_month_transactions_2020 AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS transaction_date,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start_date,
  CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_deposit_flag,
  CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_withdrawal_flag,
  txn_amount AS amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date >= '2020-01-01' AND txn_date <= '2020-12-31'
),
customer_month_balances AS (
SELECT
  a.customer_id,
  a.month_start_date,
  a.month_label,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.is_deposit_flag = 1 THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END)
           - SUM(CASE WHEN t.is_withdrawal_flag = 1 THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) AS month_end_balance
FROM all_customers_months_2020 a
LEFT JOIN customer_month_transactions_2020 t
  ON a.customer_id = t.customer_id
  AND a.month_start_date = t.month_start_date
GROUP BY
  a.customer_id,
  a.month_start_date,
  a.month_label
)
SELECT
  high.month_label AS month_with_highest_positive_count,
  high.positive_count AS highest_positive_customer_count,
  high.avg_balance AS average_month_end_balance_for_highest_month,
  low.month_label AS month_with_lowest_positive_count,
  low.positive_count AS lowest_positive_customer_count,
  low.avg_balance AS average_month_end_balance_for_lowest_month,
  (high.avg_balance - low.avg_balance) AS difference_between_averages
FROM
  (
    SELECT month_start_date, month_label,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 END) AS positive_count,
           AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM customer_month_balances
    WHERE month_start_date >= '2020-01-01' AND month_start_date <= '2020-12-01'
    GROUP BY month_start_date, month_label
    ORDER BY positive_count DESC, month_start_date ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS high
CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT month_start_date, month_label,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 END) AS positive_count,
           AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM customer_month_balances
    WHERE month_start_date >= '2020-01-01' AND month_start_date <= '2020-12-01'
    GROUP BY month_start_date, month_label
    ORDER BY positive_count ASC, month_start_date ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS low

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH monthly_nets_per_customer AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
           WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
           ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) END AS overall_percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5_percent,
  SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS numerator_customers,
  COUNT(*) AS denominator_customers
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- identify most recent month's closing and prior month's closing (prior = 0 if none)
    CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance ELSE NULL END AS most_recent_closing_balance,
    COALESCE(LAG(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 0) AS prior_month_closing_balance,
    -- compute growth_rate per customer (we compute only for rn=1 rows)
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(LAG(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 0) = 0
        THEN CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance * 100.0 ELSE NULL END
      ELSE
        CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN (closing_balance - COALESCE(LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 0)) / COALESCE(LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 1) ELSE NULL END
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      month_start,
      monthly_net,
      SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC) AS rn
    FROM monthly_nets_per_customer
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
) s

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH balances_on_first_of_month AS (
SELECT
  su.user_id AS user_id,
  se.event_time AS balance_date,
  CAST(NULL AS REAL) AS balance
FROM
  shopping_cart_users AS su
JOIN
  shopping_cart_events AS se
  ON su.cookie_id = se.cookie_id
WHERE
  strftime('%d', se.event_time) = '01'
)
SELECT
  strftime('%Y-%m', date(balance_date, '+1 month')) AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END) AS previous_month_total_balance
FROM balances_on_first_of_month
GROUP BY date(balance_date)
HAVING date(balance_date) > (
  SELECT MIN(date(balance_date)) FROM balances_on_first_of_month
)
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_daily_balances AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id, txn_date
  ) AS daily_balance
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_nonneg AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.date,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY d.customer_id ORDER BY d.date ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND 0 FOLLOWING) = 30
    THEN MAX( (SUM(daily_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY d.customer_id ORDER BY d.date ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND 0 FOLLOWING)) / 30.0, 0 )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS rolling_avg_30_nonneg
FROM customer_daily_balances d
WHERE 1=1
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(customer_month_max) AS monthly_sum_of_max_30day_avg_balances
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', r.date) AS month,
    MAX(r.rolling_avg_30_nonneg) AS customer_month_max
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_nonneg r
  JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(date)) AS first_month
    FROM customer_daily_balances
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) fm
    ON r.customer_id = fm.customer_id
  WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', r.date) <> fm.first_month
  GROUP BY r.customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', r.date)
) per_cust_month
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- parse txn_date to YYYY-MM-DD
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    txn_amount,
    txn_type
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- get customer date ranges
cust_range AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(min(txn_date)) AS start_date,
    date(max(txn_date)) AS end_date
  FROM txns
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- all transaction days per customer with net change (treat deposits positive, withdrawals negative if txn_type indicates)
cust_txn_net AS (
  SELECT
    t.customer_id,
    date(t.txn_date) AS txn_date,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN lower(t.txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit','cr','in','buy') THEN t.txn_amount
          WHEN lower(t.txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw','debit','dr','out','sell') THEN -t.txn_amount
          ELSE t.txn_amount
        END) AS net_change
  FROM txns t
  GROUP BY t.customer_id, date(t.txn_date)
),
-- generate calendar days for each customer within their range
cust_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    cr.customer_id,
    date(cr.start_date, '+' || (n.n) || ' days') AS day
  FROM cust_range cr,
       (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
        UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
        UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
        UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
        UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
       ) n
  WHERE date(cr.start_date, '+' || (n.n) || ' days') <= cr.end_date
),
-- attach net change per day (0 if no txn)
cust_day_change AS (
  SELECT
    cc.customer_id,
    cc.day AS day,
    IFNULL(ctn.net_change, 0) AS net_change
  FROM cust_calendar cc
  LEFT JOIN cust_txn_net ctn
    ON cc.customer_id = ctn.customer_id AND cc.day = ctn.txn_date
),
-- compute running balance per customer per day: cumulative sum of net_change ordered by day.
-- SQLite doesn't have built-in window framing with partition order in older versions; use correlated subquery
cust_day_balance AS (
  SELECT
    cdc.customer_id,
    cdc.day,
    -- cumulative sum up to and including this day
    (SELECT SUM(net_change)
     FROM cust_day_change cdc2
     WHERE cdc2.customer_id = cdc.customer_id
       AND date(cdc2.day) <= date(cdc.day)
    ) AS raw_balance
  FROM cust_day_change cdc
),
-- replace negative balances with zero
cust_day_balance_nonneg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    day,
    CASE WHEN raw_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE raw_balance END AS balance
  FROM cust_day_balance
),
-- month key
cust_day_month AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    day,
    substr(day,1,7) AS month -- YYYY-MM
  FROM cust_day_balance_nonneg
),
-- per customer-month maximum daily balance
cust_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    cdm.customer_id,
    cdm.month,
    MAX(cdbn.balance) AS max_daily_balance
  FROM cust_day_month cdm
  JOIN cust_day_balance_nonneg cdbn
    ON cdm.customer_id = cdbn.customer_id AND cdm.day = cdbn.day
  GROUP BY cdm.customer_id, cdm.month
)
-- final: sum per month across customers, ordered ascending
SELECT
  month AS month,
  SUM(max_daily_balance) AS monthly_total_max_daily_balance
FROM cust_month_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH events_filtered AS (
SELECT
  -- event_id: construct stable id from visit_id + sequence_number (keeps PK-ish from source)
  visit_id || ':' || CAST(sequence_number AS TEXT) AS event_id,
  event_type,
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id AS product_id,
  cookie_id AS user_id,
  event_time AS timestamp,
  shopping_cart_events.page_id AS page_id,
  visit_id AS session_id,
  NULL AS quantity,
  NULL AS other_event_metadata
FROM shopping_cart_events
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
  ON shopping_cart_events.page_id = shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id
WHERE
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id IS NOT NULL
  AND shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
),
product_event_flags AS (
SELECT
  ef.event_id AS event_id,
  ef.product_id AS product_id,
  ef.user_id AS user_id,
  ef.timestamp AS timestamp,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_view,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_add_to_cart,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type IN (3,4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_cart_removal_or_abandon,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_purchase
FROM events_filtered ef
),
product_action_counts AS (
SELECT
  product_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_view = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS view_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_add_to_cart = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_cart_removal_or_abandon = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS left_in_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_purchase = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchase_count
FROM product_event_flags
GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  view_count,
  add_to_cart_count,
  left_in_cart_count,
  purchase_count
FROM product_action_counts
ORDER BY product_id

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.

Identify the top 10 and bottom 10 interest categories based on their highest composition values across all months. For each category, display the time(MM-YYYY), interest name, and the composition value
rows.pred_sql:
WITH interest_monthly_compositions AS (
  SELECT
    im.id AS interest_id,
    im.interest_name AS interest_name,
    imt.month_year AS month_date,
    imt.composition AS composition_value
  FROM interest_metrics AS imt
  JOIN interest_map AS im
    ON imt.interest_id = im.id
),
interest_monthly_compositions_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    imc.interest_id AS interest_id,
    imc.interest_name AS interest_name,
    -- month_year is stored like '07-2018' already; if not, try to normalize safely
    CASE
      WHEN instr(imc.month_date, '-') > 0 THEN imc.month_date
      ELSE printf('%02d-%04d', CAST(strftime('%m', imc.month_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%Y', imc.month_date) AS INTEGER))
    END AS month_mm_yyyy,
    CAST(imc.composition_value AS REAL) AS composition_value_num
  FROM interest_monthly_compositions imc
),
-- top 10 composition values across all interest-month rows
top10 AS (
  SELECT composition_value_num
  FROM interest_monthly_compositions_normalized
  WHERE composition_value_num IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY composition_value_num DESC
  LIMIT 10
),
-- bottom 10 composition values across all interest-month rows
bottom10 AS (
  SELECT composition_value_num
  FROM interest_monthly_compositions_normalized
  WHERE composition_value_num IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY composition_value_num ASC
  LIMIT 10
),
top_rows AS (
  SELECT month_mm_yyyy AS time, interest_name, composition_value_num AS composition
  FROM interest_monthly_compositions_normalized
  WHERE composition_value_num IS NOT NULL
    AND composition_value_num >= (SELECT MIN(composition_value_num) FROM top10)
),
bottom_rows AS (
  SELECT month_mm_yyyy AS time, interest_name, composition_value_num AS composition
  FROM interest_monthly_compositions_normalized
  WHERE composition_value_num IS NOT NULL
    AND composition_value_num <= (SELECT MAX(composition_value_num) FROM bottom10)
)
SELECT * FROM top_rows
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM bottom_rows
ORDER BY composition DESC, interest_name, time

rows.question: Analyze the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin by region, computed as the total dollar amount spent divided by the total quantity purchased each year, excluding the first year's data for each region. Then, for each year, rank the regions based on these average purchase prices, and calculate the annual percentage change in cost for each region compared to the previous year.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH raw_purchases_year_region AS (
SELECT
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_id AS purchase_id,
  COALESCE(bitcoin_members.region, bitcoin_transactions.ticker, NULL) AS region,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', substr(bitcoin_transactions.txn_date, -4) || '-' || 
       printf('%02d', CASE 
         WHEN instr(bitcoin_transactions.txn_date, '-') = 3 THEN substr(bitcoin_transactions.txn_date, 1, 2)
         ELSE NULL END) || '-01') AS INTEGER) AS purchase_year,
  (bitcoin_transactions.quantity * 1.0) * (1.0) AS dollars_spent,
  bitcoin_transactions.quantity AS quantity_purchased,
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_time AS purchase_timestamp
FROM bitcoin_transactions
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members ON bitcoin_transactions.member_id = bitcoin_members.member_id
WHERE bitcoin_transactions.quantity IS NOT NULL
  AND bitcoin_transactions.quantity != 0
  AND bitcoin_transactions.txn_id IS NOT NULL

annual_region_totals AS (
SELECT
  region,
  purchase_year,

FROM raw_purchases_year_region
GROUP BY region, purchase_year
)

  region,
  total_dollars_spent,
  total_quantity_purchased,
  total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased AS average_price_per_bitcoin,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY purchase_year ORDER BY (total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) DESC) AS region_rank_within_year,
  CASE
    WHEN LAG(total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY purchase_year) IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ((total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) - LAG(total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY purchase_year))
         / LAG(total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY purchase_year)
  END AS pct_change_from_previous_year
FROM annual_region_totals
WHERE purchase_year IS NOT NULL

  AND total_quantity_purchased <> 0

rows.question: Using the "bitcoin_prices" table, please calculate the daily percentage change in trading volume for each ticker from August 1 to August 10, 2021, ensuring that any volume ending in "K" or "M" is accurately converted to thousands or millions, any "-" volume is treated as zero, only non-zero volumes are used to determine the previous day's volume, and the results are ordered by ticker and date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH prices_date_filter AS (
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS date,
  volume AS raw_volume
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE market_date >= '2021-08-01' AND market_date <= '2021-08-10'
),
volume_normalized AS (
SELECT
  p.ticker AS ticker,
  p.date AS date,
  CASE
    WHEN p.raw_volume = '-' THEN 0.0
    WHEN substr(p.raw_volume, -1, 1) = 'K' THEN CAST(replace(substr(p.raw_volume, 1, length(p.raw_volume)-1), ',', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
    WHEN substr(p.raw_volume, -1, 1) = 'M' THEN CAST(replace(substr(p.raw_volume, 1, length(p.raw_volume)-1), ',', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
    ELSE CAST(replace(p.raw_volume, ',', '') AS REAL)
  END AS volume
FROM prices_date_filter p
),
prev_non_zero_and_pct_change AS (
SELECT
  v.ticker AS ticker,
  v.date AS date,
  v.volume AS volume,
  (
    SELECT vn.volume
    FROM volume_normalized vn
    WHERE vn.ticker = v.ticker
      AND (
        -- compare dates as text assuming same format; pick the max prior date
        vn.date < v.date
      )
      AND vn.volume IS NOT NULL
      AND vn.volume > 0
    ORDER BY vn.date DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS previous_non_zero_volume,
  CASE
    WHEN (
      SELECT vn2.volume
      FROM volume_normalized vn2
      WHERE vn2.ticker = v.ticker
        AND vn2.date < v.date
        AND vn2.volume IS NOT NULL
        AND vn2.volume > 0
      ORDER BY vn2.date DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN (
      SELECT vn3.volume
      FROM volume_normalized vn3
      WHERE vn3.ticker = v.ticker
        AND vn3.date < v.date
        AND vn3.volume IS NOT NULL
        AND vn3.volume > 0
      ORDER BY vn3.date DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE
      ((v.volume - (
        SELECT vn4.volume
        FROM volume_normalized vn4
        WHERE vn4.ticker = v.ticker
          AND vn4.date < v.date
          AND vn4.volume IS NOT NULL
          AND vn4.volume > 0
        ORDER BY vn4.date DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )) / (SELECT vn5.volume
        FROM volume_normalized vn5
        WHERE vn5.ticker = v.ticker
          AND vn5.date < v.date
          AND vn5.volume IS NOT NULL
          AND vn5.volume > 0
        ORDER BY vn5.date DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )) * 100
  END AS pct_change_volume
FROM volume_normalized v
)
SELECT
  v.ticker,
  v.date,
  v.volume,
  p.previous_non_zero_volume,
  p.pct_change_volume
FROM volume_normalized v
JOIN prev_non_zero_and_pct_change p
  ON v.ticker = p.ticker
 AND v.date = p.date
ORDER BY v.ticker ASC, v.date ASC

rows.question: For veg whsle data, can you generate a summary of our items' loss rates? Include the average loss rate, and also break down the count of items that are below, above, and within one standard deviation from this average.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH valid AS (
  SELECT
    CAST("whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS REAL) AS loss_rate
  FROM veg_whsle_df
  WHERE "whsle_px_rmb-kg" IS NOT NULL
    AND trim("whsle_px_rmb-kg") <> ''
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(loss_rate) AS average_loss_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(*) <= 1 THEN 0.0
      ELSE sqrt( SUM((loss_rate - avg_loss)*(loss_rate - avg_loss)) / COUNT(*) )
    END AS stddev_loss_rate,
    COUNT(*) AS total_count
  FROM (
    SELECT loss_rate, (SELECT AVG(loss_rate) FROM valid) AS avg_loss
    FROM valid
  )
)
SELECT
  s.average_loss_rate,
  s.stddev_loss_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.loss_rate < (s.average_loss_rate - s.stddev_loss_rate) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_below_one_std,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.loss_rate >= (s.average_loss_rate - s.stddev_loss_rate) AND v.loss_rate <= (s.average_loss_rate + s.stddev_loss_rate) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_within_one_std,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.loss_rate > (s.average_loss_rate + s.stddev_loss_rate) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_above_one_std,
  s.total_count
FROM valid v CROSS JOIN stats s

rows.question: Analyze the average percentage change in sales between the 12 weeks before and after June 15, 2020, for each attribute type: region, platform, age band, demographic, and customer type. For each attribute type, calculate the average percentage change in sales across all its attribute values. Identify the attribute type with the highest negative impact on sales and provide its average percentage change in sales.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- define date ranges
params AS (
  SELECT
    date('2020-06-15') AS ref_date,
    date('2020-06-15','-12 weeks') AS before_start,
    date('2020-06-15','-1 day') AS before_end,
    date('2020-06-15') AS after_start,
    date('2020-06-15','+12 weeks','-1 day') AS after_end
),
-- normalize cleaned_weekly_sales.week_date to ISO (try common formats); assume week_date is YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-like.
sales AS (
  SELECT
    cw.*,
    date(substr(week_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(week_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(week_date,1,2)) AS wd_iso
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales cw
),
-- filter only rows in either before or after windows
filtered AS (
  SELECT s.*
  FROM sales s
  JOIN params p
    ON (date(s.wd_iso) BETWEEN p.before_start AND p.before_end)
     OR (date(s.wd_iso) BETWEEN p.after_start AND p.after_end)
),
-- helper to sum sales by attribute and period
attr_period_sums AS (
  SELECT
    'region' AS attribute_type,
    region AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY region

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'platform' AS attribute_type,
    platform AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY platform

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'age band' AS attribute_type,
    age_band AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY age_band

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'demographic' AS attribute_type,
    demographic AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY demographic

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'customer type' AS attribute_type,
    customer_type AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY customer_type
),
-- compute percentage change per attribute value, excluding zero sales_before
attr_pct AS (
  SELECT
    attribute_type,
    attribute_value,
    sales_before,
    sales_after,
    ((sales_after - sales_before) * 1.0 / sales_before) * 100.0 AS pct_change
  FROM attr_period_sums
  WHERE sales_before <> 0 AND sales_before IS NOT NULL
),
-- compute average percentage change per attribute type
attr_type_avg AS (
  SELECT
    attribute_type,
    AVG(pct_change) AS average_percentage_change
  FROM attr_pct
  GROUP BY attribute_type
)
-- final: list all attribute types with averages and the most negative one
SELECT
  attribute_type AS attribute_type,
  average_percentage_change AS average_percentage_change,
  (SELECT attribute_type FROM attr_type_avg ORDER BY average_percentage_change ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_negative_attribute_type,
  (SELECT average_percentage_change FROM attr_type_avg ORDER BY average_percentage_change ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_negative_average_percentage_change
FROM attr_type_avg
ORDER BY attribute_type

rows.question: Provide a detailed web sales report for each region, including the number of orders, total sales amount, and the name and sales amount of all sales representatives who achieved the highest total sales amount in that region (include all representatives in case of a tie).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH order_regions AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.total_amt_usd AS order_amount,
    a.sales_rep_id,
    r.name AS region
  FROM web_orders o
  JOIN web_accounts a ON o.account_id = a.id
  JOIN web_region r ON a.sales_rep_id IS NOT NULL AND r.id = a.sales_rep_id  -- map account's sales_rep to region id via web_region.id
  -- Note: if region should come from web_region linked to web_accounts.sales_rep_id; adjust if region sourcing differs
),
region_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    region,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count,
    COALESCE(SUM(order_amount),0) AS total_sales_amount
  FROM order_regions
  GROUP BY region
),
rep_region_sales AS (
  SELECT
    orr.region,
    a.sales_rep_id AS rep_id,
    wr.name AS rep_name,
    COALESCE(SUM(orr.order_amount),0) AS rep_sales_amount
  FROM order_regions orr
  JOIN web_accounts a ON a.sales_rep_id = orr.sales_rep_id
  JOIN web_sales_reps wr ON wr.id = a.sales_rep_id
  GROUP BY orr.region, a.sales_rep_id, wr.name
),
region_max_sales AS (
  SELECT
    region,
    MAX(rep_sales_amount) AS max_rep_sales
  FROM rep_region_sales
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT
  ra.region AS region,
  ra.order_count AS order_count,
  ra.total_sales_amount AS total_sales_amount,
  rrs.rep_name AS top_sales_rep_name,
  rrs.rep_sales_amount AS top_sales_rep_amount
FROM region_aggregates ra
JOIN region_max_sales rms ON ra.region = rms.region
JOIN rep_region_sales rrs ON rrs.region = rms.region AND rrs.rep_sales_amount = rms.max_rep_sales

rows.question: Which university faculty members' salaries are closest to the average salary for their respective ranks? Please provide the ranks, first names, last names, and salaries.university
rows.pred_sql:
WITH faculty_rows AS (
SELECT
  FacNo AS faculty_id,
  FacRank AS rank,
  FacFirstName AS first_name,
  FacLastName AS last_name,
  FacSalary AS salary
FROM university_faculty
),
avg_salary_per_rank AS (
SELECT
  fr.rank AS rank,
  AVG(fr.salary) AS avg_salary
FROM faculty_rows fr
GROUP BY fr.rank
),
faculty_distance_to_rank_avg AS (
SELECT
  fr.faculty_id AS faculty_id,
  fr.rank AS rank,
  fr.first_name AS first_name,
  fr.last_name AS last_name,
  fr.salary AS salary,
  ar.avg_salary AS avg_salary,
  ABS(fr.salary - ar.avg_salary) AS abs_diff,
  (SELECT MIN(ABS(fr2.salary - ar2.avg_salary))
     FROM faculty_rows fr2
     JOIN avg_salary_per_rank ar2 ON fr2.rank = ar2.rank
     WHERE fr2.rank = fr.rank
  ) AS min_abs_diff_for_rank,
  CASE WHEN ABS(fr.salary - ar.avg_salary) = (
     SELECT MIN(ABS(fr3.salary - ar3.avg_salary))
     FROM faculty_rows fr3
     JOIN avg_salary_per_rank ar3 ON fr3.rank = ar3.rank
     WHERE fr3.rank = fr.rank
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_min_tie
FROM faculty_rows fr
JOIN avg_salary_per_rank ar ON fr.rank = ar.rank
)
SELECT rank, first_name, last_name, salary
FROM faculty_distance_to_rank_avg
WHERE abs_diff = min_abs_diff_for_rank
ORDER BY rank ASC

rows.question: Using a Salary Dataset where the salary values need to be cleaned by removing non-numeric characters and converting them to a numeric type, write a detailed SQL query that identifies the top 5 companies by average salary in each of Mumbai, Pune, New Delhi, and Hyderabad, then compares each company’s average salary in those cities to the overall national average salary. The final result should display four columns: Location, Company Name, Average Salary in State, and Average Salary in Country, listing only the top 5 companies in each of the specified locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH raw_rows_sel AS (
  SELECT
    "index" AS row_id,
    "CompanyName" AS company_name,
    "Location" AS location,
    "Salary" AS raw_salary
  FROM "SalaryDataset"
  WHERE "Location" IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
     OR 1=1
),
-- helper to strip non-digits using nested replace for common characters (₹ , / yr and commas and spaces)
-- note: SQLite has no regexp_replace, so remove known non-digit characters and keep digits only by removing common symbols
cleaned AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    company_name,
    location,
    -- remove currency symbol, commas, spaces, slashes, "yr" and any dots; then cast to integer/real
    NULLIF(
      TRIM(
        REPLACE(
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                  REPLACE(raw_salary, '₹', ''),
                ',', ''),
              '/yr', ''),
            '/ Year', ''),
          'yr', ''),
        ' ', '')
      ), '') AS raw_digits
  FROM raw_rows_sel
),
numeric AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    company_name,
    location,
    CASE
      WHEN raw_digits GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN CAST(raw_digits AS REAL)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS salary_num
  FROM cleaned
),
per_company_location AS (
  SELECT
    location,
    company_name,
    AVG(salary_num) AS avg_state_salary
  FROM numeric
  WHERE salary_num IS NOT NULL
    AND location IN ('Mumbai','Pune','New Delhi','Hyderabad')
  GROUP BY location, company_name
),
national_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(salary_num) AS avg_country_salary
  FROM numeric
  WHERE salary_num IS NOT NULL
),
-- rank companies per location by average salary using correlated count (works in SQLite)
top5_per_location AS (
  SELECT pcl.*
  FROM per_company_location pcl
  WHERE (
    SELECT COUNT(*) 
    FROM per_company_location pcl2
    WHERE pcl2.location = pcl.location
      AND (pcl2.avg_state_salary > pcl.avg_state_salary
           OR (pcl2.avg_state_salary = pcl.avg_state_salary AND pcl2.company_name < pcl.company_name))
  ) < 5
)
SELECT
  t.location AS Location,
  t.company_name AS "Company Name",
  ROUND(t.avg_state_salary, 2) AS "Average Salary in State",
  ROUND(n.avg_country_salary, 2) AS "Average Salary in Country"
FROM top5_per_location t
CROSS JOIN national_avg n
ORDER BY t.location ASC, t.avg_state_salary DESC
